events.title: The Gregorian calendar begins
events.description: Pope Gregory XIII introduced the Gregorian calendar to correct drift in the older Julian system. In Italy, Poland, Portugal and Spain, the day after October 4 was October 15, so ten days vanished from the calendar.
events.significance: This reform created the calendar now used across most of the world.

events.title: Union victory at the Second Battle of Corinth
events.description: A two-day battle ended with Union forces under General William Rosecrans holding Corinth, Mississippi. Confederate troops under General Earl Van Dorn failed to take the town.
events.significance: Holding the rail junction at Corinth helped the Union keep control of key transport routes in the western theater of the American Civil War.

events.title: Work begins on Mount Rushmore
events.description: Sculptor Gutzon Borglum began carving the monument in the Black Hills of South Dakota. The project eventually became a huge granite portrait of four U.S. presidents.
events.significance: Mount Rushmore became one of the best-known landmarks in the United States and a symbol of national memory.

events.title: Sputnik 1 launches the Space Age
events.description: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth. The small metal sphere circled the planet and sent out radio beeps that people around the world could pick up.
events.significance: The launch started the Space Race and changed global politics, science education and technology.
